A1.justification: Both complete, readable PDFs describe the same multimodal contrastive-learning work despite the changed title and revised method. Corresponding theoretical results, experiments, figures, and Appendices A–C support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original CC3M/CC12M pretraining experiments, zero-shot and linear classification results, and repeated-evaluation results in Tables 1–6.

after.justification: V2 reports original weighted-point-cloud experiments, zero-shot and linear classification results, and weight/kernel ablations in Tables 1–3, with additional uncertainty reporting in Table 5.

M1.justification: V1 implements uniform averaging of point representations and leaves architectures with learned weights as future work. V2 implements learned signed weights through additional projection heads, uses weighted vector and random Fourier feature sums, and bounds weights with a tanh activation (Section 5.3, Algorithm 1, Appendix A.1). This changes the representation and similarity computation, beyond introducing the WPCE name.

E1.justification: CC3M and CC12M pretraining remain. V2 adds Aircraft, Flowers, EuroSAT, DTD, and Pets, removes MNIST, and adds ImageNet linear classification. Evaluation expands from nine zero-shot and eight linear-classification benchmarks to thirteen for each, including new remote-sensing and texture domains.

E2.justification: CLIP and its before-projection linear baseline remain. V1's cossim ◦ mean comparator disappears from the main comparisons; v2 adds positive-weight WPCE and WPCE Linear controls in Table 3. These are changed controls, not renamed versions of uniform mean pooling.

E3.justification: Reported CC3M training changes from 64 to 50 epochs, batch size 384 to 2048, and weight decay 0.2 to 0.5; CC12M batch size changes from 4096 to 2048. Training RFF dimension increases from 512 to 1024, and linear-evaluation dimension from 256 to 512. Linear evaluation replaces momentum SGD with validation-tuned, regularized L-BFGS logistic regression and adds WPCE before-projection features. Caltech-101 evaluation changes from top-1 to mean per-class accuracy.

E4.justification: V2 introduces dedicated tests of signed versus positive weights and mixed versus linear-only kernels (Section 6.4), plus qualitative training-stability investigations motivating its stabilizers. V1's uniform-mean control and coefficient-by-coefficient performance grid are no longer reported. The existing analysis of sensitivity to RFF randomness is retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report five zero-shot evaluations varying RFF randomness, means in the main tables, and standard deviations in the appendix. Both use a single fixed RFF realization for linear evaluation. V2 does not introduce uncertainty over independent pretraining runs, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: The result tables are extensively replaced for revised models, protocols, and coverage, including new CC12M IMQ and WPCE before-projection results. For example, v2's CC3M before-projection averages are 73.66 for WPCE IMQ and 72.14 for CLIP. These are newly reported results, not same-setting gains over v1. V2 also contains conflicting CC12M CIFAR-10 values: Gaussian/IMQ score 77.64/79.46 in Table 1 but 46.77/45.59 in Table 5.

T1.justification: The principal theorems, excess-risk bounds, weighted-class approximation guarantee, and proof strategies are retained. V2 corrects the missing logarithm in the PMI definition in Assumption C.2(d) and changes the printed RFF normalization from sqrt(1/(2D)) to sqrt(2/D), with an unbiased-estimator derivation in Appendix A.1. These are localized mathematical corrections.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion redefine the central contribution around implemented weighted point cloud embeddings and connect the retained approximation theorem to that proposal. V1's operational proposal uses uniform point sets and explicitly reserves weighted architectures for future work. The underlying PMI and downstream-classification claims remain.

C2.justification: The central PMI and representation-capacity interpretation remains. V2 adds interpretations of negative weights and nonlinear kernels, tentatively attributes nonlinear-only training failure to vanishing gradients, and explains weight divergence and temperature saturation. Its linear-classification discussion now distinguishes two feature settings and acknowledges the Gaussian/CC3M exception, replacing v1's explicit discussion of the gap to before-projection CLIP.

D1.justification: V2 adds weight-head stabilization and inverse-temperature parameterization details, expanded RFF implementation guidance, cuML and regularization-search specifications, and dataset split counts in Table 4. These go beyond relocating existing settings into Appendix A. Conversely, v2 reports kernel-search ranges without identifying the selected settings as explicitly as v1 and omits v1's specific FP16/BF16 choices.

R1.justification: V2 adds Chen et al. (2024) on CLIP transfer and Zhai et al. (2024) on RKHS-based analysis, alongside new dataset and optimization references. It removes the related-work paragraph on auxiliary-loss extensions and associated citations. The main positioning relative to contrastive-learning theory and alternative similarities remains.

P1.justification: V2 retitles the paper and substantially rewrites the abstract, motivation, and conclusion around WPCE. It removes the introduction's contribution list, reorganizes Section 5 around the weighted formulation, theorem, and implementation, and moves the algorithm and substantial implementation material into Appendix A. This is extensive narrative restructuring.

P2.justification: Figures 1–2 are revised to depict weights and weighted embeddings. Separate CC3M/CC12M result tables become grouped displays, new ablation and dataset-split tables appear, and the uncertainty tables are consolidated. Algorithm 1 moves to the appendix with a revised, numbered presentation. These substantially change the visual organization beyond numerical updates.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially narrows v1's acknowledged gap between its weighted-class theorem and its uniformly weighted implementation by implementing and testing learned signed weights. Targeted ablations, broader domain coverage, and before-projection comparisons for both WPCE and CLIP strengthen support for the actual proposal; localized mathematical corrections improve accuracy. The conflicting CIFAR-10 entries and less explicit selected hyperparameters remain reporting weaknesses, but the gains in methodological coherence and empirical support are substantial.
